# Pixels {#sec-pixels}

::: {.callout-note}
This chapter is planned: it states the question and the method. Results will replace the plan as the
analysis is done.
:::

A pixel is the smallest place on the canvas where people meet. Its history is a sequence of colours, each
placed by someone, each lasting until someone else paints over it.

## The question

How long does a colour survive on a pixel, and what decides it? A placement that repairs an artwork should last;
an attack should be undone quickly. The survival time of a colour is the simplest measure of conflict that needs no
labels.

## Why it matters

Survival times are the r/place version of *revert* statistics in Wikipedia edit wars (*studied under another name*;
Yasseri et al. 2012, see @sec-reading), where reverts signal conflict and their timing shows memory and burstiness.
If pixel overwrites behave like reverts, r/place becomes a spatial member of a well-studied family.

## Plan

The test of whether the cooldown changes behaviour is pre-registered in
[`prereg/03-cooldown-switches.md`](https://github.com/TheChesireCat/rplace-2017/blob/analysis/prereg/03-cooldown-switches.md),
committed before any of its outcomes was computed.


- For each placement, the time until the pixel next changes colour (censored at the end of the event).
- Kaplan–Meier survival curves, split by whether the new colour matches the colour two steps back (an "undo").
- **Null:** the same placements with times shuffled within each pixel, which keeps how busy each pixel is and removes
  any memory.
